Menu Cart 0 Fuzz Pedals Crunch Overdrive Products Video Demos Press Our Story Special Orders Contact Log in Create account Fuzz Pedals Crunch Overdrive Products Video Demos Press Our Story Special Orders Contact Home › The Cozmic Fuzzball McGregor Pedals The Cozmic Fuzzball Regular price $185.00 USD Sale price Unit price / per Shipping calculated at checkout. Default Title - $185.00 USD Quantity Add to Cart     Not a vintage fuzz clone. The Cozmic Fuzzball runs fuzz → distortion → overdrive in series—a hybrid you morph with one knob. Attack at minimum is overdrive only; turn up Attack to layer distortion in front, then fuzz in front of that. Hand-soldered in British Columbia for guitar and bass. ▶ Watch video demos | Read the Vintage Guitar review → | Press release Why players choose the Cozmic Fuzzball Original circuit — not another Fuzz Face spin; designed to inspire new tones, not replicate old ones One knob, three textures — Attack blends overdrive, distortion, and fuzz in a single cascade Touch-sensitive — responds to picking dynamics, volume knob, and pickup output Tracks fast passages — sustains and follows scalar lines without turning to mud Quiet for a fuzz — low noise with clean power; high-impedance input (doesn’t have to be first in chain) Hand-soldered in BC — true bypass, top-mounted jacks, LED brightness trim How Attack works — signal flow The Cozmic Fuzzball is three stages in series: fuzz → distortion → overdrive . Attack at minimum: Overdrive only—the back of the chain Attack up: Distortion is layered in front of the overdrive Attack further up: Fuzz is layered in front of the distortion (and overdrive) Pickup output and your guitar’s volume pot strongly affect how much fuzz comes in—hot humbuckers push into fuzz sooner; roll back for cleaner textures. Bass players: start with Attack near minimum and go from there. As reviewed in Vintage Guitar “Sweet & Gnarly” — McGregor Cozmic Fuzzball , Vintage Guitar “Straddles overdrive, distortion, and fuzz textures but never appropriates one over the other… tracks well for fast scalar passages, and is great for players hip to picking dynamics.” “Gnarly tones with musical sheen… adjusting Tone and Attack together showcases the pedal’s response with squish and a lot of sustain.” “It’s a hybrid with plenty of character, perfect for players looking to craft their own voice .” “The Cozmic Fuzzball doesn’t do metal, can’t nail Hendrix fuzz tones, and won’t take you to SRV land. What it does is something unique.” — honest expectations for pros comparing it to genre benchmarks. Video demos ▶ All McGregor Pedals demos → Controls Attack — Strength of signal into the fuzz transistor; more Attack = more fuzz and sustain. Low settings = distortion/overdrive; pinned = fuzz-land Tone — Variable high-pass filter; left = more bottom end (bass-friendly), right = guitar and bass Vol — Output after the tone filter LED brightness — Side trim pot (jeweler’s screwdriver): dark stage to bright sun How to use it Guitar starting point: Attack ~1/3 or below = mostly distortion/overdrive; bring up Attack to layer fuzz in Tone: Clockwise raises the corner frequency and rolls off lows—start around 10 o’clock on guitar and adjust. Bass : Start with Tone fully left; bring up to taste Before Crunch: Stacks well with transparent overdrive after fuzz for stacked amp-like textures Specifications Type: Hybrid fuzz / distortion / overdrive cascade (guitar & bass) Signal path: Fuzz → distortion → overdrive (Attack blends layers) Controls: Attack, Tone, Vol + LED brightness trim Input: High impedance—doesn’t have to be first in chain Bypass: True bypass Power: 9 V DC, center-negative 2.1 × 5.5 mm (Boss-style). 12–18 mA depending on LED setting Layout: Top-mounted jacks and power Built: Hand-soldered in British Columbia, Canada Batt
